co_bookend_the.blurb: The Bookend is a tall granite buttress at the west end of the Book group on Lumpy Ridge, above Estes Park. Nearly everything here is traditional, from long chimney lines and a wide crack inside the Great Dihedral to slab and face climbs. Grades start around 5.6 and reach 5.13, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.11, and several routes take multiple pitches. Climb of the Ancient Mariner and Orange Julius (both 5.10a) are the best known, while Hot Licks, Knight's Gambit and Bombay Chimney (5.8) draw steady traffic. It sees fewer parties than its neighbors, but the walk in is long, roughly 40 to 45 minutes, and reaching routes right of Orange Julius involves some scrambling. The rock is gritty, so bring a full rack.
co_bookend_the.approach: Follow the Lumpy Ridge trail west past the old Twin Owls area, continue beyond the Book and the Bookmark, then take a faint spur to the southeast prow. A little scrambling is needed to get to the routes on the right.

co_lower_grotto_wall.blurb: Lower Grotto Wall is the big south-facing granite cliff that rises right beside the Independence Pass road above Aspen, and the showpiece of the Grotto Walls. Bolted lines and crack climbs share the wall, and the grades lean hard toward 5.10 through 5.12, with a few 5.13s at the top end. Tarzan, Scene of the Crime and Espresso Love are among the standouts, and Grotto Wall Traverse and Twin Cracks give milder trad at 5.8. The face bakes on bright summer afternoons, though the left side holds shade into midday. The roadside pullout gets crowded on summer weekends, so arrive early.
co_lower_grotto_wall.parking_note: Roughly nine miles up the Independence Pass road from Aspen, a wide pullout sits on the left just after a switchback, and the wall rises directly above it.

co_in_between_egg_upper_eggs.blurb: The Eggs is a compact group of boulders in the east section of Alderfer/Three Sisters Park, in the foothills west of Denver. Most blocks stand among pines, so shade is easy to find. Problems run from VB up to V9, with the largest share between V1 and V5, which makes it a friendly first stop for newcomers and a solid circuit for mid-grade boulderers. Ground Separation is a favorite, Scoop aka Pac-man is a V7, and Tsunami (V9) marks the top of the range. The boulders sit only a short, flat walk from the trailhead, a few yards off the Hidden Fawn Trail. Bring a pad, and expect the first small lot to fill early on busy weekends.
co_in_between_egg_upper_eggs.approach: Take the Hidden Fawn Trail from the lot and bear right; the boulders appear about a half mile along, a short distance off the right side of the path. The walk is flat.

co_vault_the.blurb: The Vault is one of the cliff sections of Shelf Road, the large bolted-climbing destination north of Cañon City. The climbing here is overwhelmingly sport, with the bulk of routes between 5.10 and 5.12 and a few easier lines and a handful of trad options mixed in. Many routes carry jewel and gem names, such as 14 Carats, Family Jewels and The Gem, while Make It Rain and Splitting the Stone are good 5.11c tests. Walks at Shelf Road are generally short on established trails, and the area is popular enough that nearby campgrounds fill on good-weather weekends.

co_combat_rock.blurb: Combat Rock is a south-facing crag of about 250 feet in the Estes Park Valley, just above Big Thompson Canyon. It is mostly traditional, with discontinuous cracks, friction slabs and a few roofs, plus a handful of bolted faces. Routes are one or two pitches, so it suits a half day, and grades cluster from 5.9 to 5.11. Diagonal (5.9) is the standout two-pitch line, and Saigon to Pearl Harbor and Nuclear Polka are good 5.10 options. Flaring cracks can be hard to protect and some older lines have long gaps between gear, so bring a small rack and two ropes for the rappels. The southern exposure keeps the wall warm on clear cold days.
co_combat_rock.parking_note: From Loveland drive about 17 miles up US 34 through Big Thompson Canyon, turn right onto Devil's Gulch Road, then right again onto the dirt Storm Mountain Road. Use the pullout on the north side; there is plenty of room.
co_combat_rock.approach: A path drops into the gulch and climbs out the far side to the base of the wall.

co_lion_s_den_the_2.blurb: The Lion's Den is a cluster of small crags in the northern row of the Monastery, high in the hills above Big Thompson Canyon near Estes Park. The rock is pegmatite, steep and edgy or slabby with good friction. Nearly every route is bolted and short, and the grades are welcoming, with plenty of 5.7s and 5.8s, some 5.6s and 5.9s, and a few 5.11s such as Bear Hug on a gently overhanging prow. Trails here are faint, with loose scree and underbrush, and the layout is maze-like, but the reward is more solitude and better views than the main Monastery corridors. The hike in is long and steep, and the elevation above 8,000 feet means cloudy days can feel cold.
co_lion_s_den_the_2.parking_note: Drive Storm Mountain Drive (Colo 128) about five miles past the turnoff near Drake and park in the camping area on the left. The trailhead is a short walk further up the road, at the switchback.
co_lion_s_den_the_2.approach: The trail starts with a steep drop, then a steep climb, and passes the Guardian; the Lion's Den lies uphill and northwest of it along faint paths.

co_coney_island.blurb: Coney Island is a granite sport crag on the north side of Boulder Canyon, about nine miles up the canyon road from Boulder. Most routes are bolted, with a smaller group of trad lines and a couple of boulder problems, and grades run from 5.8 to 5.14 with the bulk between 5.10 and 5.12. Runaway (5.8) and Lucky Strikes Again (5.9, a notably steep one) are the moderate picks, while Joy Ride, Give the Dog a Bone and Die Reeperbahn serve harder climbers. Walk-ins in the canyon are short, generally 5 to 15 minutes. North-side crags in the canyon tend to stay climbable on winter days and can get hot in summer sun.

co_dude_s_throne.blurb: Dude's Throne is a small crag perched above Dude's Fishing Hole in Golden Gate Canyon State Park, at roughly 8,900 feet. It is mostly sport climbing, with a few trad cracks such as Dude's Jam Crack and a handful of boulder problems, and grades from 5.9 to 5.13 centered on 5.10 through 5.12. The crag looks small but has big routes, including Buster Brown (5.13a), Howdy Doody Time (5.11b) and Open Space Cowboy (5.12a). The main faces look southwest; the south side is sunny from about midday, while the north face, the Throne Room, stays cool when the rest is hot. There is no cell coverage.
co_dude_s_throne.parking_note: Pass through the Aspen Meadow Campground and continue to the lot at Dude's Fishing Hole; the crag is visible from the parking area.
co_dude_s_throne.approach: A climbers' trail contours through forest from the lot to the base. It can be faint in places, so watch for the climber sign and arrow.

co_pine_cone_dome.blurb: Pine Cone Dome is a granite dome near the upper end of Elevenmile Canyon, west of Lake George. From the road it can look mossy and broken, but good lines hide among the lichen and blocks. Trad and sport routes share the dome, with grades from easy fifth class to 5.12 and most falling between 5.7 and 5.10, so it works well for moderate climbers. Wrestle with the Pig (5.9) and Talk to Your Toes (5.10b) are fun sport picks, Fuzzy Wuzzy (5.10b) is a trad option, and Stories for Boys (5.11a) raises the bar. Some routes rated as beginner level feel harder than expected.
co_pine_cone_dome.parking_note: Drive to the far end of Elevenmile Canyon; the dome is the large one on the right, around mile 8. Park at the picnic area close to the trail.
co_pine_cone_dome.approach: A short trail leads up from the picnic area parking.

co_i_watch_crystal.blurb: Watch Crystal is the best-known face at East Animas, a sandstone crag on the Animas Valley's eastern flank just outside Durango. Most routes are one or two pitches, mainly traditional with bolted lines mixed in, and grades run from 5.6 to 5.13 with most between 5.10 and 5.11. Simians to the Sun (5.9+), Watch Crystal Crack (5.10d), Durangutan (5.10c) and Power Glide (5.12b) are area classics. The rock can be loose in spots and grades are often stiff, so approach with caution; doubles in cams up to hand size plus some nuts will handle most lines.
co_i_watch_crystal.approach: Watch Crystal is the first major wall on the trail up from the lot; at the fork, go right for Simians to the Sun.
